# IA drift review — three findings on /settings/billing + a stale doc link

## crime_00017 · route_metadata_drift → **warn**
`/settings/billing` is labeled five different ways: file `billing.tsx`, component `PricingPage`, `metadata.title: Plans`, `<title>: Subscription`, nav labels `Plans` / `Billing`. agent_risk 0.49, confidence 0.65. This will surface as flickering page titles, mismatched analytics events, and agents picking the wrong term when extending the page — but no runtime break. **Warn, don't block.** Require alignment in the same PR if this branch touches billing/nav; otherwise file a follow-up. Escalate to **block** only on a release PR.

## crime_00015 · duplicated_navigation_source → **warn (pair with #17)**
Same destination `/settings/billing` in `src/nav/registry.ts` ("Plans") and `src/nav/sidebar.ts` ("Billing"). This is the **root cause** of two of #17's six divergent labels — fixing the nav source of truth knocks out part of route_metadata_drift for free. Treat as one ticket with #17: pick a canonical label, collapse to one nav source (or document which is authoritative), regenerate the other. agent_risk 0.49, confidence 0.7. Same disposition as #17.

## crime_00013 · docs_code_drift → **ignore on this PR, fix opportunistically**
`docs/teams.md:5` links to `./setup.md` which doesn't exist. Severity low, blast radius is documentation-only — no users or production code follow this link. confidence 0.9 (the detector is sure the file is missing), but the cost of waiting is near zero. **Ignore for merge gating**; queue a one-liner to either restore `setup.md` or fix the link. Only escalate if `teams.md` is the canonical onboarding doc for the workspace/team flows — in which case re-bucket as a warn.

---

## Synthesis
All three findings point at the same underlying problem: **no single source of truth for IA** (routes, nav, page metadata, docs links each maintained by hand). The two `/settings/billing` findings (#17 + #15) are one bug shown from two angles and should be fixed together in a small follow-up PR — picking a canonical label and either consolidating to one nav file or deriving routes+titles from it. #13 is unrelated cleanup that fits the same theme but doesn't need to ship with them.

**Suggested gate**: block none. Warn on #17/#15 as a paired follow-up. File #13 as backlog.
